title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: M_{g,ν} (moduli multiplicity/stack of stable ν-pointed genus-g curves) is stratified by stable dual graphs. M_G is the stratum of curves of type G. A generization G → G' is a contraction of a subset of the edges of G. M*_{G,G'} is the deleted tubular neighbourhood of M_G inside the closure of M_{G'}, i.e. a small neighbourhood of M_G with the divisors at infinity not belonging to M_{G'} removed. The previous page defines its fundamental groupoid ΠM*_{G,G'} via universal coverings.

On this page (102)/(103) Grothendieck writes the 'specialization diagram for fundamental groupoids'. The horizontal arrow ΠM*_{G,G'} → ΠM_{G'} is induced by the inclusion into the open stratum M_{G'}. The vertical arrow ΠM*_{G,G'} → ΠM_G comes from the retraction of the tubular neighbourhood onto M_G; on the previous page it is noted that the inclusion into the full neighbourhood is a homotopy equivalence. He calls the vertical map φ_{G,G'} the 'homomorphism of specialization from G to G''. He also writes the target as Π(M_G, Γ_{G,G'}), where Γ_{G,G'} is the set of edges contracted.

He then studies φ on π_1. M*_{G,G'} fibres over M_G, with fibre a product of punctured disks, one for each edge to be smoothed. So the base M_G is a K(π,1) (a finite quotient of a product of moduli of pointed curves), and the fibre is a K(Z^C,1). The long exact sequence then makes ΠM*_{G,G'} a canonical 'extension' of Π(M_G, Γ_{G,G'}) by Z^C, with C the set of smoothed edges. In modern terms, Z^C is the free abelian group of Dehn multitwists along the vanishing cycles. ΠM*_{G,G'} is the stabilizer-of-multicurve type group, and φ is the map to the 'boundary' groupoid.

The next page turns this into a 'torseur de générisation' and states a transitivity property for composites G → G' → G''. This is part of Grothendieck's programme of describing the structure at infinity of the Teichmüller tower ('Lego') by gluing data between fundamental groupoids of strata.
errors: The main text says C is 'l'ens. des arêtes de G'. For the fibre structure it should be only the edges of G contracted in G' (the edges indexed by Γ_{G,G'}); the vertical marginal note seems to correct this.

The product-of-punctured-disks fibration is only literally a product after labelling the edges. Aut(G) permutes the edges, so in general Z^C is a twisted local system over ΠM_G rather than a constant group. This is presumably why the refined object Π(M_G, Γ_{G,G'}) is introduced. As stated, 'extension by Z^C' hides this twist.

ideas.what: Specialization diagram ΠM*_{G,G'} → ΠM_{G'} and ΠM*_{G,G'} → ΠM_G for strata of the boundary of moduli of curves
ideas.modern_name: Boundary/stratum fundamental groupoids of the Deligne–Mumford compactification; specialization maps; tangential base points at boundary strata
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse), developed by Ihara–Nakamura, Nakamura, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps, Lochak–Schneps
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (structure à l'infini of the Teichmüller tower, Lego), in outline only

ideas.what: Deleted tubular neighbourhood of a stratum fibres over the stratum with fibre a product of punctured disks; π_1 is an extension by Z^C
ideas.modern_name: Stabilizer of a multicurve in the mapping class group, as an extension of the mapping class group of the cut surface by the multitwist group Z^C
Strata of M̄_{g,n} are orbifold K(π,1)'s (Teichmüller theory)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (asphericity of the Teichmüller tower multiplicities)

ideas.what: Generization torsors and their transitivity for G → G' → G'' (announced on the next page)
ideas.modern_name: Gluing/cocycle data for the boundary structure of the Teichmüller tower; compatibility of tangential base point paths

missed.claim: A detailed, unpublished formulation of the 'structure at infinity' via a canonical specialization diagram for fundamental groupoids of all strata pairs (G, G'). It is set up for a transitivity/torsor formalism. This is more systematic than the sketch in the Esquisse, but its content largely matches later work by Nakamura and by Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps.
missed.quote: "diagramme de spécialisation pour les groupoïdes fondamentaux" ... comme une "extension" canonique des groupoïdes Π(M_G, ...) par Z^C
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historically documents Grothendieck's intended groupoid-level boundary formalism, which is relevant to the GT-action on the profinite Teichmüller tower. It is mathematically not new.

deep.surprise_reason: Standard topology of boundary strata: deleted tubular neighbourhoods and multitwist extensions. It is of historical interest as Grothendieck's own groupoid-theoretic set-up of the Esquisse's 'structure à l'infini', but there is no new result.
transcription_corrections: The text under the first diagram reads 'équivalence de groupoïdes' (applied to ΠM_G ≅ ΠM_{G,G'}). The label φ_{G,G'} on the vertical arrow of (103) is clear.
In the line under (103), 'lié à Π(M_G, Γ_{G,G'})' belongs to the right-hand insertion that replaces the crossed-out text.

'Les propriétés de l'homom. sur les π_1 des[...] fibration de base M_G ... fibre un produit de disques épointés (en nombre le cardinal de Γ ..., ou un produit)'. This is approximate, but the fibre is clearly a product of punctured disks.
The bottom-left NB likely reads: '(M_G, ...) est un K(π,1), et grâce aux propriétés des fibrations ... suite exacte : 0 → Z^C → ΠM* → Π(M_G, Γ_{G,G'}) → ...'.
'Arêtes' replaces the crossed-out 'flèches' ('ens. des arêtes de G').
